introduction: The Báb wrote a scripture whose stated aim was to be surpassed. “My aim in planting the Tree of the Bayan hath been none other than to enable you to recognize Me”; do not let this book, or its dignitaries, or your expectation, veil you from Him Whom God shall make manifest. Bahá’u’lláh then claims to be that One, and says the Bayán held nothing but his mention. Christians know the pattern from John the Baptist, and the readings invoke him by name: the voice in the wilderness, the one not worthy to bear the shoes, the greatest born of women who is less than the least in the kingdom, the prisoner who sends to ask “Art thou he?” Moses promised a prophet like himself, Malachi a messenger and Elijah, Jesus a Comforter, and the Qur’an has Jesus announce the Praised One. Three companions press on the difficulty of any such promise: Jesus’s warning about false Christs, his refusal to name the day where the Báb named a year, and the Seal of the Prophets, the verse by which most Muslims hold that the series is closed.
questions: “We are Moses’ disciples.” How does reading 2 use the example of earlier peoples of the Book, and what is the Báb asking of his own followers by it?
John said, “I am not the Christ”, and sent from prison to ask “Art thou he?” What do readings 15 to 25 claim the Báb knew and intended about the One to come?
Jesus warned against anyone who says “Lo, here is Christ”. How could a follower of the Báb honour both the promise of the Bayán and that warning?
The Báb speaks of One who will appear after Him Whom God shall make manifest, and another after him. What does it mean for a religion to expect its own successor?

“Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John.” Readings 6, 71 and 72 call the relation identical and yet claim more for the Báb. In what respects is it like, and unlike?

outside.why: “My aim in planting the Tree of the Bayan hath been none other than to enable you to recognize Me.” Paul says the same of an earlier law: it was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ.
A book whose purpose is another. Had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.
Look on yourselves as on those “given the Book before you”, lest you be veiled as they were. Ye search the scriptures, and they testify of me, and ye will not come to me.
The Pharisees’ answer is the veil itself: we are Moses’ disciples; as for this fellow, we know not from whence he is.
“Believe in how God maketh Himself known unto you in truth.” The Bereans received the word with readiness of mind, and searched whether those things were so.
The Báb gives glad tidings of Him Whom God shall make manifest. The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord.
John: he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear.
Zacharias over the infant John: thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways.
The Qur’an has Jesus do the same: bringing good tidings of a messenger who cometh after me, whose name is the Praised One.
Malachi: behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.
And Moses: I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren, like unto thee.

A promise of one to come invites claimants. Jesus: there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs; if they shall say, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth. How did the Báb’s own followers have to weigh his promise against this danger?
The highest excellence of the people of the Bayán lies in the word of their Lord about what is coming. Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see.

The belief of the people of Bahá about the Báb’s station. Jesus of John: among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater; notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he. The readings claim more for the Báb than this.
“We have once again sent John unto you, and He, verily, hath cried out in the wilderness of the Bayan.” I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord.
Government, clergy and leaders sought to extinguish his light. Fain would they put out the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light.
A book addressed to One not yet revealed. Simeon had waited his whole life for the consolation of Israel, and knew it in a child.
“The first to veil himself” may be one of the faithful. He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
And the first to believe may be anyone. So the last shall be first, and the first last.
No Messenger was sent nor Book revealed except for Him. All things were created by him, and for him.

The Báb looks beyond the Promised One to one after him, and another after. For most Muslims a single verse closes that door: Muhammad is the messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. What in a community’s self-understanding changes if the series does not end?

Hebrews: God, who at sundry times spake by the prophets, hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son. Every dispensation has heard its own time as the last days. What does the Báb’s open series do with that sense?
Do not be veiled from Him by the Bayán’s own dignitaries. The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
The Báb “left no veil”: the whole Bayán points to another. John confessed, and denied not; but confessed, I am not the Christ.
“He arose not but to mention Him … and breathed not but in His Cause.” I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.
Every commandment of the Bayán was made subject to His good pleasure. Think not that I am come to destroy the law: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
The Point spoke in His name and heralded His Revelation. He that seeth me seeth him that sent me.
“He is the One for Whose sake Thou hast yielded Thy life.” Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
The Báb named a year. Daniel is given numbers of days, and told: blessed is he that waiteth.
Jesus refused a date: of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven. Why would one herald fix a year and another forbid the asking?
The Báb made the One to come the centre of his teaching. Jesus at the last supper: I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter.
Earlier dispensations had a single allusion to the next. The last words of the prophets of Israel are one: behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great day.
“Shouldst Thou dismiss the entire company of the followers of the Bayan”, He would be within His right. God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
“Be patient until there passeth from the Bayan nine.” The vision is yet for an appointed time; though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come.

He shall come with truth. Deuteronomy gives Israel a test for anyone who speaks in God’s name: if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, the Lord hath not spoken it. What tests did the Báb give for the One he promised?
At His appearance nothing held back will avail. The merchant, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had.
To believe in Him is to believe in God and His verses. He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
Whoever sees Him, believing, “is presented unto God”. He that hath seen me hath seen the Father.
Fix your gaze on Him. The wise virgins took oil in their vessels with their lamps, and were ready when the bridegroom came.
Should you attain to Him, seek none other. The day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.
Ask God’s help to be ready on that day. Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning.
Heaven, earth and sea were created for no other purpose. The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way; then I was by him, as one brought up with him.
His glory is “immeasurably above every other glory”. A name which is above every name.
The Báb prays for those who will believe in Him. Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word.
“Grant me … to attain unto His presence.” One thing have I desired of the Lord: to behold the beauty of the Lord.
The sole object of all the Herald revealed was this Revelation. He expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning himself.

Exalted as the Báb’s station is, the readings place it second. John in prison sent to ask: art thou he that should come, or do we look for another? Even the herald had to ask. What does a herald know?
The relation is “identical” to that of John and Christ. Elias is come already, and they knew him not.

shortfall: Reading 4 is seventeen similar announcements in sequence, and many later readings are prayers and testimonies that repeat the title “Him Whom God shall make manifest”; companions were given to the announcement, the herald’s self-effacement, the timing, the conditions of recognition and the open succession, and not to each repetition.
